objective: Predict aggregate yes-share by Swiss municipality before federal referendum, target macro-object equal-commune MAE <=4 pp.
requirements: Each version: fixed hypothesis/configurations before scores, implementation, targeted tests, chronological matched benchmark, analysis, report, immutable run and artifact IDs, source URLs/hashes, decision. Record negative results and failed runs; don't relabel blocked stages complete.

Maintain 66-object population and reference 7.229527497606818 unless a documented comparison explicitly uses a separate matched subset. No comparison outcomes from 2023 onward in fitting, calibration, selection or scoring. Existing prepared snapshot may contain them; project filtered modeling reads only. Avoid exposed 2023+ test.

Do not infer individual voting behavior or use personal-level data. Predict public aggregate outcomes only. No political persuasion, voter targeting or recommendations about campaigning. No current-election forecasts/deployment; do not touch frozen candidate, main, production.

Publication cutoff: at least day before vote, exact source identity and timing checked. Retrospective source revisions, dates and proxies explicitly flagged, no invented values. No actual participation/ballots/outcomes as features for target date. Observed results only historical training and scoring. No same-day calibration.

Report macro-object municipal MAE, centered municipal MAE, national and canton macro-object MAE using ex-ante ballot weights for predictions, actual valid yes/no counts for observed aggregates only; also report coverage, paired-by-date interval, per-object and per-fold scores. Distinguish equal-municipality vs ballot-weighted aggregate. Do not claim comparable international scores without same metric and horizon.

If a source or tool is blocked, try reasonable alternative official sources, record exact blocker and defer rather than invent. Keep a clean staged branch and use optimistic compare-and-swap ref updates.
Use existing V8.1 datasets and artifact hashes for reference. Retain exploratory V9 as separate candidate; no automatic promotion on reused dates. No blanket claim that 4 pp is feasible.

stages.title: Vote-expectation surveys
hypotheses: Expected national yes share (not probability of majority yes) complements intention and trend
Compare expectation only, blend, regularized chronological calibration and structural fallback
stages.gate: Review exact source/object/wave/number; check publication; do not mix majority probabilities and expected shares; same geographic correction and matched metrics

stages.title: Campaign media coverage
hypotheses: Pre-vote fög coverage volume and tone provide new campaign signal
Model tone level, relative prominence, change between truly dated windows
stages.gate: Original report/date/period/label evidence; source must predate referendum; avoid post-election reports and campaign persuasion

stages.title: Participation and ballot weights
hypotheses: Historical aggregate participation model improves ex-ante national/cantonal weighting and local calibration
Compare last historical turnout, shrinkage, object-conditioned estimates, survey participation if sourced
stages.gate: No contemporaneous actual turnout as feature; validate turnout separately and vote share on same objects; include valid ballot denominator caveat

stages.title: Aggregate poststratification and multilevel regression
hypotheses: Aggregate ecological compositional models and survey margins can improve local contrasts
Compare partial pooling, regularized cross-classified aggregate models; do not pretend marginals are joint microdata
stages.gate: Use public aggregate data only; explicit identifiability and ecological assumptions; no individual vote inference

stages.title: Independent canton forecasts / small area estimation
hypotheses: Partial pooling across cantons and object features improves geographic levels; compare direct canton ridge/XGB, shrinkage, municipal bottom-up
stages.gate: Actual target canton result not an input; canton targets only historical; keep municipality forecast all rows

stages.title: Hierarchical reconciliation (MinT)
hypotheses: Joint national-canton-commune coherence using historical error covariance and ex-ante ballot weights improves forecasts
stages.gate: Fit covariance on chronological out-of-fold predictions only; regularize small sample; keep probabilities bounded and hierarchy coherent

stages.title: Hybrid Gaussian-process profiles
hypotheses: Hybrid structured object and geographic kernel plus latent profile may outperform current PCA
stages.gate: No contemporaneous commune results; compare low-rank/kernel and simple controls; actual observation-based oracle clearly separated

stages.title: Official brochure corpus and semantic effects
hypotheses: Improve V9's 16/66 validated-summary candidates via source-based mapping; extract policy direction, effects, affected institutions, cost/benefit and structured mechanisms from actual pre-vote text
stages.gate: Evidence, source date/hash, title mapping; no retrospective outcomes or assumed links; train-only compression; compare titles, summaries and effects separately

stages.title: Socioeconomic data and object × commune interactions
hypotheses: Income/housing/education/sector detail offer better exposure measures than 5 STATENT variables; explicit interactions
stages.gate: OFS/AFC official source and vintage; harmonize geography; as-of availability; no individual profiling; compare matched support

stages.title: Chronological ensemble
hypotheses: Complementary validated models reduce errors when selected by prior OOF folds; compare convex uniform/regularized stacking
stages.gate: Out-of-fold fit and nested chronology; no selection on same held-out rows; report error correlations and gain intervals

morning_report: Cumulative French report of all completed/blocked/running versions; per-version exact configurations, score tables, charts, coverage, CI, methodology, links, source caveats, remaining tasks. Update after every run. At final scheduled check report measured results, not promised scores.
